unresolved_added: Equation (2) prints 0.24 s times the three/twelve-minute difference, while Table 3 reserve values and its J/kg label imply a factor or unit-scale conflict; retain the source expression but forbid direct reuse until dimensionally reconciled.
Equation (3) uses an undefined P and Table 3 does not provide units for MAP_TTF or CP_TTF, so branch-boundary calculations are not operationally typed.
The source sets k=0.7 and A=0.1 by an asserted continuity requirement without printing their units, continuity equations, fit residuals, or uncertainty.
The aligned curves support an internal plausibility comparison only; sample size, matched profiles, source uncertainty, and external outcome validation are absent.
Summing fractions of maximal holding time assumes linear additive depletion across changing output and omits recovery below CP and path-dependent physiological state.

Mechanical transmission loss, drivetrain efficiency eta=0.95, and the terminal five-percent physiological reserve are three different interfaces and must not be merged, double-counted, or used to justify one another.
vwind is defined as wind speed but set equal to bicycle speed in no wind, so it functions as relative incident air speed in one place and ambient wind in another; direction and sign are missing.
The stated air density cannot be derived from temperature and humidity alone without pressure, and the venue/time distribution used for the value is not shown.
Cr is given only as a wide range, with no selected value or calibration for the plotted output-speed curves, preventing reproduction of rolling resistance.
The prose calls r an inner diameter while the geometry treats it like a radius; later tables also mix radius and angle fields, so the turn input convention is inconsistent.
The force sum, efficiency division, rider-mass-normalized output, and total rider-plus-bicycle mass do not receive one explicit dimensional and sign-convention closure.

The source uses total turn length relative to course length to ignore turn time and speed transitions, but short sharp turns can have nonproportional braking, acceleration, energy, and safety effects.
The strategy treats controls as section-boundary steps while Equation (10) retains acceleration and later guidance assumes finite braking; the state transition is not reconciled.
Equation (12) leaves the relationship between t and tn, control bounds, initial/final speeds, continuity, and the integration of local turn limits unspecified.
Mathematica Minimize is named without domains, starting values, precision, stopping rules, convergence status, grid size, or a discretization-refinement check.
Turn output and speed values lack units, and the reported 12.13 output for turn E cannot be checked against a duration-specific response constraint from the table alone.
Calling roughly 400 m long enough to hold an optimum is not supported by approach speed, acceleration time, braking distance, or a steady-state distance calculation.

Small-slope aggregation is motivated by approximate trigonometric linearity but no error is propagated to speed, chosen output, resource use, or completion time; Equation (14) is also visually ambiguous.

Rows labeled like #55km/#56km and values such as 0.2m, approximately 0m, 0 degrees, and 12 degrees appear under mismatched length/radius/angle fields, so Table 9 cannot be parsed as trusted parameters.
A 4.4-degree reference from section 63 is transferred to sections 24-27 without a transfer argument, while the 20 m braking and immediate recovery instructions omit acceleration constraints.
Temperature/humidity evidence from adjacent sport contexts and the claim that training mitigates rain do not close rain-related grip, braking, or safety effects for this event.
The weather sweep fixes grade at zero percent, so it cannot establish route-wide robustness on the multi-slope Belgium and Tokyo courses.
The source alternates among one-percent, ten-percent, one-to-four m/s, and plus/minus two m/s perturbations; Figure 18 appears to span roughly -27% to +34% while prose says an undefined ten percent.
The prose reports turn wind-direction and wind-speed effects near 0.1% and 0.01%, but Figure 20 reaches roughly +1.7% and -2.2%; the quantities cannot be treated as one result.
The four sine terms have no empirical frequency basis, phase, amplitude distribution, random seed, or spline boundary conditions, and three runs cannot establish general robustness.
The worst printed run is 54.38 against 53.03 minutes, about 2.55%, slightly above 'within 2.5%' and inconsistent with the Summary's 'within 2%'.
Table 10 prints specialist times 40.97/33.63, whereas Table 11 uses 56.03/34.63; 56.03 belongs to another profile in Table 10 and 34.63 differs from 33.63.
Table 11 model/champion pairs imply about 1.7% and 14.6% differences, not a shared approximately six-percent error; the claimed accuracy is not arithmetically reproducible.
A scenario calculation using average-profile inputs that lies near one champion time cannot show that the strategy causes an average athlete to achieve champion performance.
The team discussion announces a one-kilometer straight but the next page defines and reports a twenty-kilometer model, leaving the evaluation scenario inconsistent.
The 48/27/25 shares and 21.2-minute result have no printed objective, coefficient table, switch-cost model, search method, fourth-finisher state logic, or sensitivity.
A modeled 56.6 km/h value near the cited 56.1 km/h BMC speed does not prove accuracy because course, weather, riders, formation, and timing conditions are not matched.

The Anna van der Breggen/Tokyo champion/mathematician/Cambridge PhD chain requires external verification, while RIDERMAN, RIDEMAN, and RIDERMEN vary across the artifact; neither enters reusable factual evidence.
The 85/90-percent route thresholds, grade classes, hard output changes, and turning advice lack individual uncertainty and safety bounds; red/green dependence and tiny curves reduce accessibility.

No appendix or code publishes rider rows, route arrays, Webots geometry, Mathematica notebook, Python scripts, seeds, spline rule, formation coefficients, or plotted arrays, preventing end-to-end reproduction.
